title: Free a bottle jammed in a capper's infeed starwheel
instruction: The capper's infeed has jammed on a bottle and the line is stopped and locked out. Take the jammed bottle out of the starwheel and put it in the red reject bin.
context: On filling and capping lines a container pinched between a starwheel pocket and its guide rail is cleared with the machine stopped and locked out, by turning the starwheel back by hand, against the flow, until the pocket opens, then lifting the container out. Pulling it out against the pinch breaks glass (cut hands, a line clearance) or cracks the change part; turning the wheel forward wedges it harder. The direction has to be worked out from the flow arrows and the guide that closes in along the flow. Unlike TK-DA2CEU (push a peg past a hidden obstruction that must be tipped out) and TK-DPNBZR (clear a press jam by an instructed selector sequence), here the mechanism itself traps the part and must be back-driven in the one correct direction, which nobody states. Done by: packaging and filling machine operators and tenders (O*NET 51-9111.00).
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left); angles are yaw about the vertical, anticlockwise from +x seen from above. Deck: a fixed stainless steel plate 29 x 29 x 0.4 cm centred at x 31.5, y -11.5. Starwheel: a blue UHMW-PE four-pocket wheel (four lobes 8 cm long and 1.6 cm wide on a 4 cm hub, 1.5 cm thick, 250 g) on a fixed steel shaft at x 30, y -13, its underside 3 cm above the deck, turning on a friction bearing (0.06 N*m). Indexed orientation (the start, 0 deg): the lobes point at -90, 0, 90 and 180 deg (along -y, +x, +y, -x); a white painted index mark 0.4 x 3 cm on the -90 deg lobe, centred 5.5 cm from the shaft, reads against a degree scale on the deck; turning back, against the flow, is anticlockwise. Guide: six fixed stainless steel rail segments, each 3.8 cm long (tangential), 0.8 cm thick (radial) and 5 cm tall, standing on the deck round the far side of the wheel, each square to its radius from the shaft (yaw = that radius's angle). Centre x, y; yaw; inner face's distance from the shaft: 1: 38.56, -10.22; 18 deg; 8.60. 2: 37.89, -6.61; 39 deg; 9.75. 3: 34.98, -4.38; 60 deg; 9.55. 4: 31.64, -2.63; 81 deg; 10.10. 5: 27.70, -2.19; 102 deg; 10.65. 6: 23.68, -3.27; 123 deg; 11.20. Wide where bottles come in (6), closing in along the flow. Three white painted-steel chevron arrowheads on the deck, centred 14 cm from the shaft at 112, 82 and 52 deg, point clockwise round the wheel (the flow). Bottle: a white HDPE 4 x 4 cm French-square bottle, 14 cm tall with its blue PP cap, filled (150 g), standing upright, cap up, on the deck in the pocket between the 0 and 90 deg lobes: base centre at x 33.70, y -6.59 (7.4 cm from the shaft at 60 deg), yaw 60 deg (faces square to that radius), its outer face 1.5 mm off guide segment 3 and its nearest corner 1.7 mm off the 90 deg (trailing) lobe. It is pinched: it holds against 6 N until the wheel is turned back 6 deg. Reject bin: a fixed red polypropylene bin, 12 x 12 x 6 cm, centred at x 19, y -33. A grey painted-steel isolator (4 x 5 x 7 cm) with a red steel padlock and a yellow PVC lockout tag sits on the deck's far corner at x 42, y -22.5.
scoring: From the episode's recorded poses (on a real rig: the wheel's index mark against a degree scale, and video of the bottle). Latched 0 for the rest of the trial if the bottle moves 3 mm or tips 5 deg from its jam pose before the wheel has been turned back (anticlockwise, against the flow) by 6 deg, or if the wheel is ever turned 3 deg forward with the flow. Otherwise: 1.0 with the bottle upright (under 15 deg) and its whole footprint inside the bin on its floor, let go (both grippers 2.5 cm clear) and still, success when held 1 s; 0.5 with it upright, let go and still at least 5 cm from its jam pose but not in the bin; 0.25 while the wheel is turned back 6 deg or more; else 0. Scored at the last step. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0.
reset_notes: Fixed and never moved: deck, guide, chevrons, shaft, isolator and bin (bolted or doweled at the setup positions). Sim: the wheel returns to 0 deg and the pinch is re-made. Real rig: the sim's pinch is a hold on the bottle, released by the wheel's angle, not an elastic wedge (a squeeze through the lobe would itself back-drive a 0.06 N*m wheel), so it is built as a switched holding magnet: a DC holding electromagnet set flush in the deck under the bottle's base centre, a 25 mm x 1 mm mild-steel disc bonded under the bottle's base, and a latching relay that a cam flag on the wheel trips at 6.0 to 6.5 deg of back-off and only the reset button re-arms. The shaft's friction washer is set so the wheel starts turning at 0.75 N pulled at a lobe tip (0.06 N*m). Reset: (1) turn the wheel back about 10 deg; (2) stand the bottle upright, cap up, on its 4 x 4 cm outline marked on the deck (base centre x 33.7, y -6.6, yaw 60 deg), with a 1.5 mm shim between its outer face and guide segment 3; (3) turn the wheel forward to 0 (index mark on the scale's 0 line, within 0.5 deg); (4) press reset to arm the magnet; (5) remove the shim. Calibration and the release check are in the README.
fidelity: Rigid boxes, one shared friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). The starwheel is a rigid body on a PhysX revolute joint with Coulomb bearing friction (0.06 N*m). The pinch is a breakable bond (6 N) between bottle and deck that is switched off once the wheel is 6 deg back; there is no elastic wedging (a real rig uses a switched holding magnet, see reset_notes). The pocket is square-sided, the guide straight segments; no capper turret or conveyor.
